title: Heat treatment line for forged steering arms with one heating furnace for both quenching and normalizing
summary: The available technical agreement describes a roller-supported mesh belt line for steering-arm forgings. The first furnace provides heating for either normalizing or quenching.
coverAlt: Quench and temper route for forgings: loading table, shared quenching and normalizing furnace, quench tank, lift and blow-dry stage, tempering furnace, cooling tank and a second lift and blow-dry stage for collection.
coverCaption: Quench and temper route for forgings: loading table, shared quenching and normalizing furnace, quench tank, lift and blow-dry stage, tempering furnace, cooling tank and a second lift and blow-dry stage for collection.
seoTitle: Forged steering arms: one furnace for two heat treatments
seoDescription: One furnace heats forgings for normalizing or quenching. On the quench and temper route, the forgings then pass through a quench tank and tempering furnace.

presentation.status: Technical agreement text (source copy without both parties’ seals)
presentation.processCaption: The animation shows the quench and temper route. After quenching, the forgings enter the tempering furnace. The first furnace can also be used for normalizing.
presentation.note: The figure comes from the available technical agreement. Actual throughput depends on the parts, loading and process conditions.
work: Parts: forgings such as steering idler arms and pitman arms.
Treatment: quenching and tempering after forging, or normalizing the forgings.
Capacity basis: weight per hour, dependent on the forgings, the way they are loaded and the process requirements.
features: Are two front-end heating furnaces needed?
The text assigns heating for both normalizing and quenching to the same roller-supported mesh belt furnace.
How do parts leave the cooling tank?
An elevator lifts the parts out and a fan above the belt blows them dry.
The text assigns process commissioning to the buyer, with assistance from the supplier.
params: Effective width of the first furnace
presentation.supplier: The text assigns transport, installation in position, secondary wiring, equipment commissioning, and operator and maintenance training to Suneng. Suneng assists with process commissioning.
presentation.buyer: The text assigns unloading, plant-to-cabinet wiring, embedded connections, external utility lines and materials, pits and pit steps, the cooling water basin or cooling tower, commissioning media and acceptance parts to the buyer.
presentation.scope: Roller-supported mesh belt quenching and normalizing furnace, quench tank, liquid storage tank, roller-supported mesh belt tempering furnace and discharge cooling equipment.
presentation.pre: Both parties check the mesh belt, chain, controls and safety guards at the supplier's plant.
presentation.site: The available agreement lists approximately 1000 kg/h for final acceptance. The quenching furnace is checked at three points at 800 °C. The temperature deviation within the same zone must be within ±5 °C.
faq: Was this rate measured on site?
No. The available agreement lists approximately 1000 kg/h as a final acceptance condition for the steering-arm forging line. It states the rate to be checked at site acceptance.
Do normalizing and quenching and tempering follow the same downstream path?
They share the first furnace. The quench tank and subsequent tempering route described in the text are for quenching and tempering.
Who provides the cooling water source?
The buyer provides the cooling water basin or cooling tower.
